description: §8.10.4 Tier 2 loop hoisting (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): the pre-fetch keys its Map on the key column even when the user's SELECT list does not carry it bare — not selected at all (`SELECT body … WHERE id = …`), aliased (`SELECT id AS note_id, body …`), or table-qualified (`SELECT n.body FROM notes n WHERE n.id = …`). The rows the loop sees are exactly the per-iteration query's rows (`Object.keys(row)` is `body` only — the projected key is stripped), and `.get()` is the FIRST row of the per-key query in its own ORDER BY (two tags for note 7, `ORDER BY label` → `a`). Pre-S455 the Map was keyed on `_r["<keyColumn>"]`: absent / aliased / qualified, every lookup missed and every row read `not` on success ("none,none"); and `.get()` kept the LAST row per key.
rationale: §8.10.4: "The key column is the column referenced by the single equality predicate in the `?{}` template." §8.10.2: "`.get()` in the loop becomes `Map<key, Row>`; missing keys yield `not`". §8.10.3: "The rewritten loop is observationally equivalent to the un-rewritten loop".
